newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab Auto sees costs putting pressure on H2.
newsitem.headline: Saab Auto sees costs putting pressure on H2.

text.p: Car maker Saab Auto on Tuesday posted a pre-tax loss for the first half of 1997 saying costs of new products and increased marketing put pressure on profitiability which could continue this year.

"For the second half of 1997 we expect, according to what we have previously indicated, that ongoing product developments and marketing initiatives will keep pressure on profitability," Saab Automobile AB said in a statement.

Saab Auto, which is jointly owned by U.S. auto group General Motors and Swedish investment group Investor AB, posted a pre-tax loss of 600 million crowns ($74.5 million) for the six months against a loss of 428 million crowns a year earlier.
The operating loss widened to 394 million crowns from 95 million, depressing the operating margin to -3.3 percent from -0.9 percent.

"The economic result for the first half of 1997 reflects the significant efforts we have made within marketing to improve our possibilities to increase sales and raise the awareness about the brand name Saab on our key markets," company chief executive Robert W. Hendry said in the statement.

While these efforts have had a negative impact on earnings, Hendry noted increased sales on several markets, as well as structural improvement in the import and retail segments, which would be beneficial in the longterm.
Six-month sales volumes rose three percent to 50,800 cars with sharp sales increases in The Netherlands, up 37 percent, Britain, up 26 percent, Sweden, up 20 percent, and Germany, up 15 percent.
